nodes.name: ci.yml
nodes.summary: Primary CI workflow triggered on push to main and pull requests, running parallel jobs: verify (actionlint, lint, typecheck, verify:i18n, coverage tests, build), audit (pnpm audit), osv (OSV vulnerability scan), gitleaks (secret detection), and e2e (Chromium Playwright suite).
nodes.languageNotes: Five independent jobs run in parallel; the e2e job uploads a Playwright report artifact only on failure.

nodes.name: metrics.yml
nodes.summary: Scheduled daily (and manually dispatchable) workflow whose report job computes a pipeline metrics report via the metrics script and writes it to the GitHub step summary.
nodes.languageNotes: Triggered by a daily cron schedule and workflow_dispatch; reads GitHub Actions data via GH_TOKEN.

nodes.name: mutation.yml
nodes.summary: Weekly scheduled (and manually dispatchable) workflow whose stryker job runs Stryker mutation testing over lib/** and publishes the HTML mutation report as a retained artifact.
nodes.languageNotes: Cron-scheduled weekly with a 15-minute timeout; uploads the mutation report with 30-day retention regardless of outcome.

nodes.name: post-deploy-smoke.yml
nodes.summary: Workflow triggered on successful production deployment_status events; its smoke job runs the Playwright smoke suite against the live production site, uploading the report on failure.
nodes.languageNotes: Gated by a conditional on deployment_status.state == 'success' and the Production environment; targets the live production URL.

nodes.name: prod-monitor.yml
nodes.summary: Every-15-minutes scheduled monitor whose probe job runs inline curl-based HTTP probes against the production site, asserting status codes, expected body text, and security headers on key routes.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses an inline bash script with assert_status/assert_contains/assert_header helpers and a concurrency group preventing overlapping monitor runs.

nodes.name: safari.yml
nodes.summary: Cross-browser workflow whose safari job runs the Playwright WebKit/Safari E2E suite on macOS, triggered on push to main, a weekly cron, and manual dispatch.
nodes.languageNotes: Runs on macos-14 to exercise the WebKit engine with two retries; injects Resend test credentials like the Chromium e2e job.

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand what this project is: the marketing and intake site for the Agentic Engineering training programme, a bilingual (NL/EN) Next.js 15 App Router app with a dark, terminal-native aesthetic deployed on Vercel. The README lays out the stack, repo layout, the contact-form pipeline, security headers, deployment, and the i18n parity gate. It is the roadmap for everything the rest of this tour explores in code.

tour.title: Locale Routing Entry Point
tour.description: Every request first hits middleware.ts, which runs next-intl locale routing before any page renders, so visiting `/` redirects to `/nl` (the default locale). The routing rules and supported locales are declared centrally in i18n/routing.ts, while i18n/request.ts resolves the active locale per request and loads the matching message bundle. Together these form the bilingual foundation the entire UI depends on.
tour.languageLesson: next-intl middleware intercepts requests at the edge and rewrites/redirects based on a locale prefix. The matcher config keeps it off static assets and API routes, so only page navigations pay the routing cost.

tour.title: Translation Catalogs and Parity Gate
tour.description: The locale bundles loaded in Step 2 live as namespaced JSON: messages/nl.json (the primary Dutch catalog) mirrored by messages/en.json. These two files are the highest fan-in nodes in the codebase, consumed by nearly every page, component, and test. scripts/verify-i18n.ts flattens both catalogs and fails the build if their key sets diverge, preventing translation drift between the two languages.

tour.title: Root Layout and Design Tokens
tour.description: Once the locale is resolved, app/[locale]/layout.tsx validates it, sets the request locale, and wraps every page with shared Nav and Footer chrome plus per-locale metadata. app/globals.css imports Tailwind v4 and declares the dark-mode design system as @theme tokens (colors, fonts), the single source of truth for the terminal-native look defined in DESIGN.md. This layout is the frame all routes from here on render inside.
tour.languageLesson: Tailwind v4 replaces the JS config file with a CSS-native @theme block. Design tokens declared there become both CSS custom properties and Tailwind utility classes, so colors and fonts have one authoritative definition.

tour.title: The Home Page Composition
tour.description: app/[locale]/page.tsx is the localized home page, a React Server Component that assembles the marketing narrative: the Hero banner up top, the ProofStrip of social-proof pills beneath it, then the training listings and instructor grid, finishing with JSON-LD structured data for SEO. It reads its copy through the next-intl catalogs from Step 3 and renders inside the layout from Step 4, giving you a bird's-eye view of how a page is built from presentational components.

tour.title: The Training Domain
tour.description: The site's core subject matter lives in data/trainings.ts, a typed static catalogue of trainings, modules, and pricing. Two components consume it: TrainingCard renders a compact summary used in the home listing from Step 5, while TrainingDetail expands the full curriculum, outcomes, and audience, with DayAgenda showing a numbered module pill strip. This is one of the most tightly coupled clusters in the codebase, with the data module feeding cards, detail views, and tests alike.

tour.title: Instructors and the About Page
tour.description: Mirroring the training domain from Step 6, data/instructors.ts holds the typed instructor records, surfaced through InstructorCard which looks up a record and applies translated name and bio fields. app/[locale]/about/page.tsx is a server component that renders an instructor grid using these pieces, showing the same data-plus-component pattern applied to a second content type.

tour.title: The Intake Form
tour.description: ContactForm is the client-side intake form, built with react-hook-form and a Zod resolver, posting submissions to the contact API and surfacing localized validation and status messages. Its validation rules come from lib/validation.ts, the shared Zod schema and enums that define the exact shape of a valid submission. Crucially, this same schema is reused server-side in Step 9, so the client and server agree on what valid input means.

tour.title: The Contact API Pipeline
tour.description: The form from Step 8 posts to app/api/contact/route.ts, the strongest cluster in the codebase and the security-critical heart of the backend. The handler runs a defence-in-depth gauntlet: same-origin/CSRF check, per-IP rate limiting via lib/rate-limit.ts, a honeypot silent-drop, and the shared Zod schema from Step 8, before dispatching through lib/email.ts. The email lib sends via Resend and runs every header-bound field through lib/sanitize.ts to strip CRLF and block header injection.
tour.languageLesson: Next.js App Router route handlers export named HTTP-verb functions (POST) that return a Response. Validating the parsed body with Zod's safeParse keeps untrusted input from reaching side effects, and returning typed errors maps cleanly to 400/403/429/502 status codes.

tour.title: The News Article Pipeline
tour.description: Beyond the static catalogues, the site loads editorial content from the filesystem. lib/articles.ts reads markdown files from the news directory, derives slugs, and Zod-validates their frontmatter, returning articles sorted by date; lib/parseFrontmatter.ts is the small YAML-extraction helper it leans on. app/[locale]/articles/page.tsx is the server component that calls getArticles and renders the localized list, echoing the Zod-validation discipline you saw in Steps 8 and 9 applied to content.

tour.title: The SEO and Metadata Surface
tour.description: A marketing site lives or dies on discoverability, so several metadata routes round out the pages from Steps 5 through 10. app/sitemap.ts expands a fixed path list across both locales with hreflang alternates, app/robots.ts emits robots.txt rules, app/[locale]/opengraph-image.tsx generates per-locale social-share images at the edge, and JsonLd.tsx injects structured-data scripts (used on the home page in Step 5). Together they make the bilingual content legible to crawlers and social platforms.

tour.title: Security Headers and CI Capstone
tour.description: Finally, the production hardening. next.config.ts wraps the app with the next-intl plugin and attaches strict production security headers, including a Content-Security-Policy that allowlists only the origins the app actually talks to (such as the Resend API from Step 9). The CI workflow in ci.yml gates every push and PR with parallel jobs: lint, typecheck, the verify:i18n parity check from Step 3, coverage tests, a build, dependency and secret scans, and a Playwright e2e suite, automating the quality bar the whole tour has walked through.
tour.languageLesson: A Content-Security-Policy is a single header string of source directives; tightening connect-src and script-src to specific hosts limits exfiltration and injection. GitHub Actions runs the listed jobs in parallel by default, so a slow e2e job does not block fast lint/typecheck feedback.
